description: We are a team of BRAC University CSE students passionate about software, AI, ML, data analysis and space exploration. We enjoy turning real world problems into practical solutions through coding, research, visualization and teamwork. For this challenge, we are especially interested in earth science, habitats, mars, the moon and human exploration.
summary:
Mars: The Last Descent (12 KM: Beyond the Depth) is an open-source browser game built by Team BRACU Abyss, six students from Dhaka, Bangladesh, for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

For most students, space science feels distant and stuck inside flat textbooks. Our game changes that by turning real NASA missions into an interactive adventure. You play as an astronaut who has crash-landed on Mars. Your only companion is NOVA, a smart robotic cat with a built-in scanner. To repair your ship and get home, you must explore four Martian biomes and learn from eight historic NASA machines, including Apollo 11, Sojourner, Opportunity, and InSight.

Each mission teaches a real science idea through simple puzzles, such as programming rover routes with signal delay or checking Martian rocks for ancient water. Every machine unlocks three clear cards: The Machine, The Science, and Why It Matters. Players can also press N anytime to ask NOVA questions. This AI chatbot connects the Google Gemini API to live NASA InSight weather data and official NASA open datasets. By mixing gameplay with verified NASA facts, we help students experience space engineering firsthand.
details:
Mars: The Last Descent (12 KM: Beyond the Depth) is an open-source, browser-based educational space exploration game built around real NASA missions. Players take on the role of an astronaut who has crash-landed on Mars alongside NOVA, a robotic cat companion with a built-in scanner. To repair their spacecraft and return home, players explore four procedurally generated Martian biomes, use a Sonar Radar Ping ([SPACE]) to locate eight historic NASA relics (including Apollo 11 LRRR, Pathfinder/Sojourner, Opportunity, InSight, Spirit, Phoenix, Apollo LRV, and Surveyor 3), and collect 18 geological specimens.

Each mission teaches real aerospace and planetary science through interactive challenges—such as experiencing 1/6th lunar gravity, programming Sojourner's path under light-time signal delay, and inspecting Opportunity's hematite "blueberries" under a microscope. Every discovered relic unlocks three structured knowledge cards (The Machine, The Science, and Why It Matters) verified against NASA and JPL archives. Players can also press [N] anytime to open NOVA // UNIT-09, an in-game AI chatbot connecting the Google Gemini API to live NASA InSight Mars weather telemetry.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Turns Passive Memorization into Active Learning: Instead of reading flat textbook diagrams, students apply real scientific principles—passive optics, rocker-bogie mobility, communication delay, remote spectroscopy, and Martian seismology.
  • Accessible Anywhere with Zero Cost: Because the game runs directly in any modern web browser with no downloads, accounts, or heavy hardware required, it is ideal for classrooms in Bangladesh and underserved communities worldwide.
  • Future Classroom Scalability: Our open-source CC0 foundation is designed to expand with full Curiosity and Perseverance campaigns, a Bangla language mode, and teacher dashboards for school pilots.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • Frontend & Game Engine: React 19, TypeScript 5.8, Vite 5.3+, and HTML5 2D Canvas/WebGL procedural rendering (src/render/, src/world/).
  • Procedural Audio: Custom zero-dependency WebAudio API synthesizer (src/systems/audio.ts) generating footsteps, jetpack thrusters, sonar pings, cat purrs, and ambient Martian wind in real time.
  • AI & Live Telemetry: Google Gemini API integrated with live NASA InSight weather data (api.nasa.gov) and mission catalogs (data.nasa.gov, earthdata.nasa.gov/user-resources/remote-sensors).

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

  • Knowledge Repairs Your Ship (Not Scrapping Hardware): Rather than treating historic rovers and landers as junk to break apart for metal, players repair their ship by learning the engineering principles behind each machine.
  • Strict Historical Accuracy: Every mass, date, power rating, and instrument is fact-checked against official NASA, JPL, and CNES archives, and retired missions are clearly separated from active ones like Perseverance.
  • Lightweight, Self-Contained Performance: By generating terrain with multi-octave Perlin noise and synthesizing all sound effects via code instead of large media files, the game loads quickly even on low-bandwidth school connections.
